title: Per-level workload of a divide-and-conquer tree
summary: Doubling the number of subproblems while halving each subproblem's work keeps the total work per level constant.
context: Let n be a nonnegative integer power of 2. Each box in the figure represents a subproblem whose operation count equals its current size; starting from the root, every subproblem splits into two equal halves from one level to the next.
description: The right side totals the operations at each level. The bottom row draws only 4 boxes separated by ellipses to represent all n leaves. The table below describes the levels for general n; for small n, intermediate levels may be absent and the leaf level may coincide with an earlier row rather than there always being 5 fixed levels.

frames.title: Per-level workload of a divide-and-conquer tree
frames.explanation: Numbering the root as level 0, level d has 2^d (2 to the power d) subproblems performing n / 2^d operations each, whose product is always n. At the leaf level each subproblem has size 1, so 2^d = n and d = log₂ n (log base 2 of n); from level 0 through level log₂ n there are log₂ n + 1 levels in total. At the bottom of the diagram, multiplying n operations per level by the total number of levels gives n(log₂ n + 1) = n log₂ n + n, which is O(n log n).
